mechanism_narrative: Growth in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates a strong economy, leading to increased corporate earnings and higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth does not correlate with positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 6% signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative when UNRATE drops below 6%.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 grows and UNRATE decreases, it indicates a robust economy, leading to higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: No positive correlation between GDPC1 growth and UNRATE decrease on S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening, high FEDFUNDS (above 4.5%) increases borrowing costs, reducing S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns remain positive when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Increased industrial production (INDPRO) signals higher economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth does not lead to positive S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in PAYEMS (non-farm employment) indicates a strong labor market, boosting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative despite PAYEMS increase.

mechanism_narrative: Rising CPIAUCSL (inflation) and increasing FEDFUNDS indicate tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: No negative correlation between CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS on S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts (HOUST) during expansion signals economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: HOUST increase does not lead to positive S&P 500 returns.
